21 The extension of a copper wire is measured for different forces applied to the wire. A graph is
plotted to show the variation of the force on the wire against extension. The maximum force is
applied at point P.
force
R Q
P
S
extension
0
0
T
Which statement must be correct?
A
Point R is the limit of proportionality.
B
The elastic potential energy of the wire at point S is given by the area under the graph
between points T and S.
C
There is no plastic deformation between points Q and P.
D
The wire obeys Hooke’s law up to a point between R and Q.

hints: Look at the axes: force vertically against extension horizontally, starting at T at the origin and ending at maximum force at P, with S on the initial straight part.
Remember that work done to stretch the wire is the area under this force-extension graph, and while the wire is still elastic this work is stored as elastic potential energy.
Check where the graph stops being straight near S, R and Q, and ask which statements about the exact limit of proportionality and about plastic flow must be true rather than only possible.
walkthrough: Identify the diagram: from T the graph is straight up to about S, then it curves through R and Q to P, so linearity is lost somewhere around S to R.
State the energy rule: for a force-extension graph, the work done to reach an extension $x$ is $W = \text{area under } F \text{ against } x$ from zero extension to $x$.
Apply it at S: S lies on the initial straight elastic section, so the deformation is recoverable and the work done from T to S is stored as elastic potential energy.

Test the other statements for must: the exact limit of proportionality cannot be fixed at R, Hooke's law cannot be extended to between R and Q because curvature has begun, and the loading curve alone cannot prove absence of plastic deformation between Q and P.
Therefore the area between T and S must give the elastic potential energy at S. This is option B.

A.explanation: R is a marked point close to where the force-extension curve begins to bend, but the graph alone does not prove the limit of proportionality is exactly at R.

B.explanation: Work done in stretching is the area under the force against extension graph, and at S the deformation is still elastic so the work from T to S is stored as elastic potential energy.

C.explanation: The section from Q to P is curved and beyond the linear part, so plastic deformation may have started and it cannot be claimed there is none.

D.explanation: Hooke's law needs $F$ proportional to $x$, a straight line through the origin, which has already ended by S-R, so it cannot be said to hold up to between R and Q.
